record.original_question: Let K be a compact subset of Rn , n ≥ 3. For φ ∈ D, let D(φ) be a least-diameter disc containing spt φ; let d(φ) = diam (spt φ), and let kφk∗ = kφk∞ + d(φ) · k▽φk∞ . Are the following conditions equivalent for continuous functions f : Rn → R? (1) There exists a sequence {fn }∞ 1 of functions harmonic near K, such that fn → f uniformly on K. (2) There exists a function n such that n(δ) decreases to 0 as δ decreases to 0, for which Z f δφ dx ≤ η(d(φ))kφk∗ C(D(φ) − X). Rn Here C denotes the harmonic capacity of Rn obtained from the kernel r −n+2 . Note that (1) implies (2), and that (2) implies (1) if f is a C 2 -function. The condition (2) is formally analogous to one that occurs in rational approximation theory. (A. G. O’Farrell)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge 3$. Let $\mathcal{D}$ denote the space of $C^\infty$ test functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with compact support. For $\varphi\in\mathcal{D}$, let $D(\varphi)$ be a closed ball of least diameter containing the support $\operatorname{spt}\varphi$, let $d(\varphi)=\operatorname{diam}(\operatorname{spt}\varphi)$, and set
$$\|\varphi\|_*=\|\varphi\|_\infty+d(\varphi)\,\|\nabla\varphi\|_\infty.$$
Let $C$ denote the harmonic capacity in $\mathbb{R}^n$ associated with the Riesz kernel $r^{-n+2}$; for a Borel set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $C(E)$ is the standard Newtonian capacity.

For a continuous function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ consider the following two conditions:

(1) There exists a sequence $\{f_m\}_{m=1}^\infty$ of functions, each harmonic on some open neighborhood of $K$, such that $f_m\to f$ uniformly on $K$.

(2) There exists a function $\eta:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ with $\eta(\delta)\downarrow 0$ as $\delta\downarrow 0$ such that for every $\varphi\in\mathcal{D}$,
$$\left|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\,\Delta\varphi(x)\,dx\right|\le \eta(d(\varphi))\,\|\varphi\|_*\,C(D(\varphi)\setminus K).$$

It is known that (1) implies (2), and that (2) implies (1) when $f$ is of class $C^2$. Determine whether (1) and (2) are equivalent for arbitrary continuous functions $f$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work by O'Farrell on capacities in function theory and on rational/harmonic approximation on compact sets, but no source directly resolving the stated equivalence between condition (1) (uniform approximability on $K$ by functions harmonic near $K$) and the capacitary distributional condition (2) for general continuous $f$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge 3$, was found. Status appears unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Capacities in Function Theory — A. G. O'Farrell
status_evidence.snippet: O'Farrell discusses capacities and analogues used to characterize approximation problems, but does not give a uniform-on-K characterization for harmonic approximation in R^n via the stated condition.
status_evidence.claim: Related framework exists but does not resolve the equivalence in question.

status_evidence.title: Transactions AMS Vol. 228 (1977), O'Farrell
status_evidence.snippet: Concerns Lip(α) rational approximation on compact subsets of C, formally analogous to the harmonic case raised here.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous rational-approximation results are known; the harmonic R^n version of the equivalence is not established here.
